questions.q: What three questions does this lesson say a real access audit has to answer?
options: Who touched the object, what they did to it, and when/how often
Which warehouse ran the query, its cost, and its duration
Which edition the account is on, its region, and its cloud provider
The table's row count, byte size, and clustering key
questions.explain: The lesson defines an audit as answering who, what (read/write), and when/how-often — turning a one-off curiosity into a real investigation.

questions.q: Why does the lesson use LATERAL FLATTEN against base_objects_accessed?
options: base_objects_accessed holds a semi-structured array; FLATTEN unpacks it into rows so you can filter to one specific object by name
FLATTEN converts VARIANT columns into VARCHAR automatically
LATERAL FLATTEN is required to query any ACCOUNT_USAGE view, even flat ones
It merges QUERY_HISTORY and ACCESS_HISTORY into one result set
questions.explain: base_objects_accessed is a semi-structured array of accessed objects; LATERAL FLATTEN turns each array entry into its own row so a WHERE clause can filter on one object's name.

questions.q: What does a non-null policies_referenced value on an ACCESS_HISTORY row tell you?
options: At least one masking or row access policy evaluated for that query
The query was run by a user without any granted roles
The query failed due to a policy violation
The table involved has never had any policy applied, ever
questions.explain: policies_referenced records which masking/row access policies actually evaluated for a query — proof the policy fired, not just that it exists.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what separates a one-off audit query from an actual governance practice?
options: Defining the question precisely, scheduling it (e.g. with a Snowflake Task), and reviewing the output on a cadence
Running the query faster by using a larger warehouse
Writing the query in Python instead of SQL
Granting ACCOUNTADMIN to everyone who needs to run it
questions.explain: A query run once during an investigation is a one-off; scheduling it and reviewing results consistently is what turns it into a repeatable practice.

questions.q: Which column would you check to confirm whether a masking policy actually applied to a specific past query?
options: policies_referenced on ACCESS_HISTORY
execution_status on QUERY_HISTORY
deleted_on on GRANTS_TO_USERS
row_count on ACCOUNT_USAGE.TABLES
questions.explain: policies_referenced is the ACCESS_HISTORY column specifically built to record which policies evaluated for a query — the direct answer to 'did it actually apply.'
